title: A Counter struct
prompt:
Create a `Counter` struct that remembers a number.

- `Counter::new()` starts at 0
- `increment(&mut self)` adds 1
- `add(&mut self, amount: i32)` adds `amount` (it can be negative)
- `get(&self) -> i32` returns the current value

```text
let mut c = Counter::new();
c.increment();
c.add(10);
c.get()  -> 11
```
hints: The struct needs one field, for example `value: i32`.
`new` has no `self` - it builds and returns a `Counter { value: 0 }`. Methods that change the counter take `&mut self`; `get` only reads, so it takes `&self`.
Inside a method, change the field with `self.value += 1;`. The last expression of `get` (no semicolon) is the returned value.
explanation: `&mut self` lets a method change the struct, `&self` only reads it. `new` has no `self`, so it is called with `Counter::new()`. Each `Counter` keeps its own value.
